los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the male genitalia and groin, demonstrating appropriate technique, communication, and respect for patient privacy and dignity
los.html:
1Explain, consent, chaperone, privacy; examine standing then lying.
2. InspectSkin, penis (hypospadias, discharge, ulcers, warts), scrotum (swelling, redness, asymmetry), groin (hernias: ask to cough).
3
  • Palpate each testis between thumb and two fingers: size
  • Consistency
  • Lumps (can you get above it? separate from the testis?)
  • Epididymis (behind)
  • Spermatic cord (vas deferens).
4Transilluminate any swelling (hydrocele glows; solid tumours don't).
5. HerniasInguinal (above and medial to the pubic tubercle) vs femoral (below and lateral); reducible?
6Inguinal lymph nodes.
FindingSuggests
Hard, painless lump in the testisTesticular cancer → urgent ultrasound, 2-week-wait
Fluid swelling around the testis, transilluminatesHydrocele
"Bag of worms" above the testisVaricocele (left)
Tender epididymis, fever, dysuriaEpididymo-orchitis
Sudden pain, high-riding horizontal testisTorsion: emergency
Can't get above it, cough impulseInguinoscrotal hernia

los.text: Perform a full cranial nerve examination and interpret clinical findings.
los.html:
NerveTest
I OlfactoryAsk about smell
II OpticAcuity (Snellen), fields (confrontation), pupils (direct, consensual, RAPD), fundoscopy, colour (Ishihara)
III, IV, VIEye movements in an "H"; diplopia, nystagmus, ptosis
V TrigeminalSensation V1–V3, jaw muscles (clench, open against resistance), corneal reflex
VII FacialRaise eyebrows, close eyes tightly, puff cheeks, show teeth; forehead sparing = UMN
VIII VestibulocochlearWhisper test, Rinne's, Weber's
IX, XSay "ahh" (uvula deviates away from the lesion), gag (optional), swallow, voice
XI AccessoryShrug shoulders, turn head against resistance
XII HypoglossalTongue: wasting, fasciculation, deviates towards the lesion

los.text: Perform a structured A to E (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) assessment on a patient presenting with chest pain.
los.html:
Chest pain A–E
A, B: oxygen only if sats <94%
C: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes, IV access, bloods (troponin), BP both arms (dissection), heart sounds
D: pain score, glucose
E: calves (PE), abdomen
ACS treatment: aspirin 300 mg, GTN, morphine (with antiemetic) if needed; STEMI → primary PCI (within 120 min)
Differentials: ACS, aortic dissection, PE, pneumothorax, pericarditis, oesophageal rupture

los.text: Manage a cardiac arrest scenario, including initiating basic life support and using a defibrillator appropriately.
los.html:
1Recognise arrest: unresponsive, not breathing normally; call the arrest team (2222), note the time.
2Start CPR 30:2 immediately; attach the defibrillator pads as soon as it arrives.
3. Rhythm check(pause <5 s)Shockable → shock then CPR 2 min; non-shockable → CPR 2 min.
4. AirwayAdjuncts, bag-valve-mask, supraglottic device; oxygen; IV/IO access.
5. DrugsAdrenaline 1 mg (immediately for non-shockable; after the 3rd shock for shockable, then every 3–5 min), amiodarone 300 mg after 3 shocks.
6Reversible causes (4 Hs, 4 Ts); swap compressors every 2 minutes; check DNACPR status.
7. ROSCABCDE, 12-lead ECG, oxygen to 94–98%, treat the cause (PCI), post-resuscitation care.

los.text: Differentiate between cardiac rhythms that require defibrillation and those that do not, demonstrating accurate rhythm recognition and appropriate decision-making in emergency situations.
los.html: • Shockable vs non-shockable rhythms: see ICM Year 1 › Emergencies & A–E › LO 27 (VF and pulseless VT are shockable; asystole and PEA aren't).

los.text: Safely perform defibrillation in accordance with current clinical guidelines, demonstrating correct use of equipment and adherence to safety protocols during resuscitation.
los.html: • Safe defibrillation: see ICM Year 1 › Emergencies & A–E › LO 28 (pad position, charge during compressions, "stand clear, oxygen away", shock, resume CPR immediately).
